author: Mark Atwood
text:
Fixed. The proof IS reachable through hickory's public API -- the bead's open question answered in the affirmative, so no upstream gap here.

NoRecords is #[non_exhaustive] but its fields are public: soa: Option<Box<Record<SOA>>> and authorities: Option<Arc<[Record]>>, the latter documented upstream as 'important to preserve for DNSSEC validation'. Record carries proof as a public field (not a method -- that tripped me up once). So classify_lookup_error now destructures NetError::Dns(DnsError::NoRecordsFound(..)) instead of calling is_no_records_found, and negative_answer_status reads the proofs off the SOA and the authority section.

Mapping, with the safety direction load-bearing: Secure only when there is at least one proof and every one of them is Proof::Secure. Any Bogus -> Bogus, any Insecure -> Insecure, nothing to inspect -> Indeterminate. A single failed proof outranks any number of good ones, because the denial is only as strong as its weakest link, and reporting Secure for an unvalidated denial would let a stripped response pass as a deliberate absence -- the attack DANE exists to stop.

Acceptance criteria:
[x] A signed NODATA yields Secure with no records, so is_authenticated_denial is true
[x] An unsigned or unvalidatable negative answer still yields Insecure / Indeterminate / Bogus, never Secure
[x] Tested -- but as unit tests over synthesised NoRecords values rather than against a live signed zone. That is deliberate: the mapping is the part that can be wrong, it covers all six proof combinations including the mixed ones, and it runs in CI with no network. A live test would exercise hickory's proof assignment rather than our mapping, and could not run on a contributor laptop.

Both directions mutation-verified: loosening Secure to 'any proof Secure' fails the safety test, and reverting to always-Indeterminate fails the capability test.

pkix-dane-resolver 0.3.0 -- a negative answer can now report Secure where it always reported Indeterminate, which a strict consumer could be matching on.
